newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea warns Seoul of "blood for blood".
newsitem.headline: North Korea warns Seoul of "blood for blood".

text.p: North Korea threatened "merciless retaliation" against South Korea on Saturday over the deaths of more than 20 of its soldiers who came ashore from a submarine last month.

"Our retaliation will be merciless," the official Korea Central News Agency (KCNA) said. "Blood should be paid for blood," the agency added in the most harshly-worded threat so far over the submarine incident.
Of the 26 North Koreans who landed on an east coast beach, 22 have been killed by Southern troops or found dead, one has been captured alive and a hunt is on for three others.
Pyongyang has demanded the return of the submarine, found grounded on rocks on September 18, along with the survivors and the bodies of the dead crew.

"The South Korean puppets should be held responsible wholly for any form of our retaliation," the agency said. "We will make them pay for their crimes a thousandfold by just means and method, when an occasion comes."

On Wednesday Pyongyang army officers had warned of "serious consequences" in a border meeting with representatives of the U.S.-led United Nations Command, which monitors the ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Earlier, the North had threatened to retaliate "a hundredfold or a thousandfold".

In its Saturday despatch, KCNA also ridiculed the United States over a separate case involving a Korean-born American working for the U.S. Navy who has been accused of passing secret documents to Seoul.
"The U.S. is now in a miserable position because it cannot but team up with such political hooligans as the South Korean puppets," it said.
"It is widely known to the world that the U.S., hand in glove with the puppets, has conducted information-gathering and subversive activities and smear campaign against (North Korea)," it added.
North Korea maintains its submarine drifted south after developing engine problem while on a training mission.

South Korea says it was dropping off armed commandos in a prelude to wider military action. In response to the incident and to the North's subsequent threats it has increased security at airports, ports and diplomatic missions and assigned more bodyguards to key public figures.
Vigilance has also been stepped up on five west coast islands seen as vulnerable to North Korean attack.
Earlier on Saturday KCNA had accused Seoul of "groundless slander" for suggestions that North Korea was involved in the killing of a South Korean diplomat in Russia's Far East.
"Although they connect the death of the puppet consul with the North in a far-fetched way, they can convince no one," the state agency said.
"The South Korean puppets are groundlessly slandering the North."
South Korea has never formally accused North Korea of involvement in the murder of its consul in the Russian Far East city of Vladivostok on Tuesday.
But South Korean media have pointed accusing fingers at Pyongyang, saying it is making good on retaliation threats.

Choi Duck-keun, who was responsible for North Korean affairs and security at the Vladivostok consulate, was stabbed and bludgeoned to death on the stairs outside his apartment by unidentified assailants.
His body arrived back in Seoul in an aircraft on Saturday accompanied by his bereaved wife and son.
